title: Scheduled jobs that run exactly when they should
summary: Replace a single server's crontab with something that survives restarts and never pays anyone twice.
context: Nandi Freight has 90 jobs in the crontab of one machine: invoices, settlement files, reminders. When it was replaced last month, some jobs never ran for two days, and no one noticed until a customer asked.
Moving to several machines is the obvious step, but some jobs must not run twice: one of them sends money to carriers. Some take seconds, and some take three hours.
must_handle: A job runs even if the machine meant to run it dies.
A job that sends money does not run twice.
A missed run is noticed, and a person hears about it.
A long job and a short job do not get in each other's way.
Teams can add a job without asking anyone for a server.
show_in_answer: What holds the schedule, and how a run gets claimed.
What happens when a worker dies halfway through.
How a job is made safe to repeat, using the money job as the example.
How missed and failing runs are noticed.
